summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by recurrent marginal (gastrojejunal anastomotic) ulcers, postsurgical nonabsorption, and refractory hypoglycemia managed with continuous gastrostomy tube feeds presented with four days of recurrent epigastric pain, nausea, and dark yellow emesis similar to prior ulcer flares, along with increased but noninfected-appearing G-tube drainage. She was hemodynamically stable with normal labs and lactate; chest and abdominal radiographs showed no free air or obstruction (with mild to moderate stool burden). She was treated medically with IV fluids, IV pantoprazole, antiemetics, and analgesia; once imaging ruled out perforation, continuous tube feeds were resumed while she remained NPO, and she had no hypoglycemia during the admission. Symptoms improved without further vomiting, and she was discharged home ambulatory with ongoing ulcer therapy (including sucralfate and an absorbable outpatient acid-suppressing regimen), PRN pain control, bowel regimen, and surgical clinic follow-up.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
